memory_candidates.content: When porting an abstract 'DerivExcludes'/prime_set_exclusion argument sketch from a research report into Lean, check for a leading case-split on head explosion (bot in the head theory) before trusting the sketch's DerivExcludes discharge to go through unconditionally: boxInv(Set.univ) = Set.univ makes the naive exclusion base (e.g. boxInv H union {A}) trivially inconsistent when H itself explodes, which the l=[] case of DerivExcludes then falsifies. Handle it with the exploding segment as a direct trivial witness in a leading by_cases, before attempting the main Zorn-based construction. This gap recurred identically in three separate instantiations (cs5_diam_witness, and canonical FCsym_box/FC4') within the same task (509), suggesting it is a structural feature of fallible-world (quasi-prime, not prime) canonical model constructions generally, not a one-off.

In Lean 4 with the module system (public/private sections), a public def cannot reference a private def in its VALUE even within the same file/module -- this restriction applies to def (Type/data-valued) but NOT to theorem (Prop-valued, proof-irrelevant), where a public theorem can freely call a private def in its proof term. Symptom: 'Unknown identifier X / A private declaration X (from the current module) exists but would need to be public to access here', raised specifically when the referencing declaration is a def, not when it is a theorem. Fix: either make the dependency non-private, or restructure so only theorems (not defs) cross the public/private boundary.
